gap: No result ChatGPT got states, for the 2-bay Synology it recommended (DS225+) and the DS425+, what Synology's own spec page says: the DS225+ has no M.2 NVMe slot, and on the DS425+ 'creating M.2 storage pools requires the use of Synology-verified SSDs'. So ChatGPT's own advice to put app data such as Audiobookshelf's /config SQLite database on an NVMe SSD works with an ordinary NVMe drive only on the UGREEN DXP2800, where the M.2 slots can form a separate SSD storage pool.
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT cited and the top results. audiobookshelf.org/docs/.../docker (cited) already says /config must be on the same machine and not on a network share, or the database will be corrupted. calibre-web.com (cited) already says Calibre-Web needs an existing Calibre library containing metadata.db, that ebook-convert is not in the container by default, and that LinuxServer's Calibre mod targets x86-64. ai-uk.ugreen.com's beginners guide (cited) already says 'The DH2300 does not support Docker or virtual machines'. racksandwatts.com/guides/best-nas-for-a-homelab-2026 (cited in chat 3) already lists the DS225+ as '2 SATA, no NVMe' and says new M.2 storage pools on the DS925+ need drives from the compatibility list, but it does not cover the DS425+ or tie this to app databases. So every 'does the plan work at all' fact is already on a cited page. Two things are new but only partly: the Synology-verified M.2 rule as it applies to the DS425+, and the fact that Calibre-Web Automated creates the library for you (calibre-web.com tells readers to import into Calibre desktop first).
decides: It backs the DXP2800 as the value pick. Of ChatGPT's three picks, it is the only one where the 'SSD for app data' step works with any off-the-shelf NVMe drive. On the DS225+ that step can't be done because it has no M.2 slot. On the DS425+ it means buying Synology-verified SSDs. None of this blocks the plan: Audiobookshelf only needs /config on local storage, and NAS hard drives count as local. For ARM boxes: the DH2300 is ruled out (no Docker). The DH4300 Plus can run Calibre-Web Automated, whose latest image ships for arm64, but the LinuxServer conversion mod is x86-64 only.

findings.label: M.2 storage pool rule
findings.value: 2 × M.2 2280 NVMe SSD slots; 'Creating M.2 storage pools requires the use of Synology-verified SSDs'
findings.note: Quoted from the spec footnotes. The same page also says 'SSD cache can be enabled with select compatible SSD'.

findings.label: CPU / RAM
findings.value: Intel Celeron J4125 (4C/4T, 2.0/2.7 GHz); 2 GB DDR4 non-ECC, 1 slot, max 6 GB (2 GB + 4 GB)

findings.label: Drive bays / M.2
findings.value: 2 × 3.5" SATA HDD or 2.5" SATA SSD; no M.2 NVMe slot listed
findings.note: The spec page lists no M.2 slot. It lists 2 GB DDR4 (max 6 GB), a Celeron J4125, and 1 × 1GbE + 1 × 2.5GbE.

findings.label: M.2 slot use
findings.value: 2 × M.2 NVMe usable as an HDD read/write cache or as a separate SSD storage pool 'which suits Docker containers, databases'; RAM 8 GB DDR5-4800, one SO-DIMM, UGREEN supports 16 GB
findings.note: Starry Hope, published 2026-09-28. Neither it nor a search turned up any SSD-brand restriction. UGREEN's own product pages returned HTTP 429 when I tried to open them.

findings.value: /books = 'Where your preexisting calibre database is located'; the universal-calibre DOCKER_MODS conversion is '#optional & x86-64 only'; the image itself ships x86-64 and arm64

findings.label: Calibre-Web Automated: library creation and architectures
findings.value: 'If you don't have an existing library, CWA will automatically create one'; the latest image is published for amd64 and arm64 (last updated 2026-09-28)

The README also says NETWORK_SHARE_MODE=true turns off SQLite WAL because 'Some network filesystems (NFS/SMB) do not fully support WAL or reliable file locking'.
